races.name: Sigeric Ltd Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Maximum Offers
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning from 91-day break but Gavin Sheehan's tactical nous and good ground form (1W2P) makes the layoff less concerning over this stamina trip.
runners_data.comment: Third on soft ground at Wincanton; these conditions should be more to his liking
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground hurdle winner; jumped better on second run over fences when third on soft ground at Wincanton (3m1f; first-time cheekpieces) and these conditions should be more to his liking; off for three months but should have every chance.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Potter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying just 156lbs with Luke Scott's 3lb claim, race-fit from 12-day turnaround and coming off solid second on good ground at this distance.

runners_data.name: Jullou De Grissay
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner with class edge but Charlie Longsdon's woeful 0/13 recent form is a significant red flag despite Sam Twiston-Davies in the saddle.

races.paceDynamic: Maximum Offers appears the most natural pace-setter in this three-runner field, with both Moonlit Potter and Jullou De Grissay likely to track close behind given their prominent tendencies. The small field and lack of confirmed front-runners means Maximum Offers can dictate terms without pressure, setting a steady gallop over this stamina-testing 3m1f trip. With all three runners comfortable racing prominently, this becomes a tactical affair where positioning into the straight matters less than who has the most left in the tank. This controlled pace scenario strongly favours horses with the best recent form and tactical speed, as the race will likely be won by whoever can quickest from the final fence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maximum Offers Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Maximum Offers gets an uncontested lead and dictates a steady gallop
scenarios.body: The 91-day break becomes irrelevant as Gavin Sheehan can time his effort perfectly from the front, with the horse's good ground form (1W2P from 3 starts) proving decisive. His superior OR of 108 and Jamie Snowden's 4/24 recent strike-rate support this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moonlit Potter Recent Form
scenarios.trigger: If the 12-day turnaround proves an advantage and Luke Scott's claim reduces the burden effectively
scenarios.body: Moonlit Potter's recent second at this trip on good ground shows he's in form, and the 11lb weight advantage over Maximum Offers could prove telling in a slowly-run finish. The combination of race fitness and Dr Newland's patient approach makes him dangerous late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jullou De Grissay Class
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a true stamina test and Sam Twiston-Davies can exploit gaps from off the pace
scenarios.body: Despite Charlie Longsdon's poor 0/13 recent record, this horse won over course and distance last year and has the class edge with 1W3P on good ground. His tactical positioning behind the other two could pay dividends if they go too fast early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Maximum Offers goes too fast early or makes jumping errors under pressure from the other two
scenarios.body: The small field dynamic breaks down with all three going too hard, turning it into a lottery where the horse who conserves most energy or gets the best jump at crucial fences prevails. Weight differentials become crucial in a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Maximum Offers must settle early - if Gavin Sheehan lets him bowl along too freely in the first mile, the 91-day break will catch up over 3m1f
Moonlit Potter's jumping under pressure from Luke Scott's inexperience - any mistake at a crucial fence could end his chances with the small field offering limited recovery options
Jullou De Grissay's early positioning will reveal tactics - if Sam Twiston-Davies drops him out back early, it suggests confidence in his stamina reserves
Weather changes affecting the going description - any softening would significantly alter the form lines for all three runners
The pace through halfway - if they crawl early in this small field, it becomes purely about who has most tactical speed from the final fence

runners_data.name: Chosen Bae
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from out-of-form Ryan Potter yard, hard to fancy on recent evidence

races.paceDynamic: Churchman and Shesupincourt are the natural early leaders, but Churchman's prominent style and recent good form makes him the likely pace-setter with Shesupincourt potentially tracking. With only two genuine pace angles in an 8-runner field, the early gallop will be reasonable but not punishing over this 2m3½f trip. The lack of genuine speed means the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, allowing horses to travel comfortably into the straight. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a finishing kick, as the moderate early pace will leave plenty in reserve for those coming from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate as expected with Churchman setting reasonable fractions
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop allows the hold-up brigade to travel sweetly and produce their best finishing kicks. Maestro Du Mesnil, Geordies Betty, and Tara Iti all benefit from being able to unleash late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Churchman gets soft fractions and isn't pressured by Shesupincourt early
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows Churchman to conserve energy and maintain his gallop to the line. His recent good form on similar ground gives him the edge when allowed an easy lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and creates a stop-start rhythm
scenarios.body: The stuttering gallop disrupts the finishing kicks of the hold-up horses and creates a tactical mess. Those who can adapt quickest or sit closer benefit from the confusion.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Shesupincourt decides to press Churchman from the start creating genuine pace
scenarios.body: The unexpected strong gallop finds out both leaders and sets up the race for a closer tracker. However, this seems unlikely given both horses' recent running patterns.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Churchman gets an uncontested lead as his recent placed efforts suggest he could finally break his maiden tag
Monitor the early pace between Churchman and Shesupincourt as any genuine speed battle would transform the race dynamics
Observe Maestro Du Mesnil's jumping rhythm early as improvement from his promising recent form could make him dangerous
Check if Brave Move shows any ring-rust signs given his 126-day absence from action
Watch for any market moves on the hold-up horses as the pace setup clearly favours their running style

races.paceDynamic: Hellion is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will be allowed to dictate terms without pressure from the gate. Crystal Days and Dinkys Rose may take prominent positions but neither is aggressive enough to challenge Hellion's lead. This creates a controlled tempo where the pace-setter can coast through the middle sections before quickening late. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours hold-up horses who can capitalize on a sustainable gallop and finish strongly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hellion sets uncontested fractions and the pace becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to position perfectly and unleash finishing kicks that the pace-setters cannot match. American Empire, Gaelic Saint, and Arctic Voyage benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If Crystal Days and Dinkys Rose apply more pace pressure than expected
scenarios.body: A genuine tempo develops that stretches the field and favors horses positioned handy who can kick from the front half of the field. Crystal Days holds every chance while Good For You could benefit from the stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapse benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Hellion sets funeral fractions and no one challenges until too late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where raw ability matters more than positioning, potentially suiting horses with untapped potential. Fidendum's Market Rasen form and Latin's flat speed could prove decisive in a messy finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front runner steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Hellion's wind operation has transformed his stamina and he can sustain the kick
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader finds enough in the tank to repel all challengers despite his moderate hurdles form to date. His previous wind issues may have masked his true ability over this trip.

watchPoints.text: Hellion could steal this if allowed completely uncontested fractions as the sole pace-setter
American Empire's 169-day break and wind surgery recovery need monitoring for fitness levels
Crystal Days represents the main prominent threat if the pace develops more genuinely than expected
Several runners making hurdles debuts or returning from long breaks could be underprepared
The going remains good throughout the card but watch for any late changes affecting hold-up horses

runners_data.spotlight: 3-13 over hurdles; only his fourth start as a chaser when too strong for two rivals over 2m at Chepstow a month ago (soft; 3lb lower); this quicker ground won't bother him at all and neither might the longer trip; good claims.

runners_data.name: Insurrection

runners_data.comment: 3m2f too far last time; can look a hard ride so the cheekpieces could be significant
runners_data.spotlight: Back to his winning trip over fences after failing to defy some serious stamina doubts over the 3m2f of the Kim Muir; he's none too consistent and looked a hard ride at Musselburgh the run before (2m4f), but he's realistically handicapped if he can travel kinder in the new cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Coastguard Station
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid course record but faces tactical disadvantage in small field where early positioning becomes crucial.

races.paceDynamic: Insurrection will set a steady, sustainable pace from the front with no other committed leaders in this small field. Numitor and Sherborne will track prominently behind the leader, while Black Hawk Eagle and Coastguard Station are likely to be held up at the rear given their hold-up styles. With only one genuine pace-setter and a field of five, this sets up as a tactical affair that could develop into a sprint finish. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers who can track Insurrection and have first run on the hold-up horses when the pace inevitably quickens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Sherborne or Numitor can sit second/third and kick when Insurrection comes under pressure.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the prominent runners to conserve energy and time their challenge perfectly. Hold-up horses face too much ground to make up when the sprint begins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Insurrection gets an easy lead and the field fails to organise a serious challenge until too late.
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds an unassailable advantage over 2m5f, with chasers unable to reel him in despite his inconsistency. The tactical runners leave their move too late in the small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawling affair until the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Black Hawk Eagle or Coastguard Station benefit from an extremely slow tempo that negates the advantage of prominent positioning. The race becomes a pure stamina test where the freshest finisher wins.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Insurrection Leads Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the other runners completely fail to lay up with the leader and allow him to dictate completely.
scenarios.body: The Paul Nicholls runner gets such an easy time in front that his class tells despite recent poor form. The field spreads out with no serious challenges materialising.

watchPoints.text: Insurrection must be watched for how easily he gets to the front - if unopposed he could steal this despite poor recent form.
Black Hawk Eagle's jumping under pressure given this is only his fourth chase start and he'll need to be accurate when making his move.
Sherborne's ability to handle the 7lb penalty after his Ascot win - any signs of the burden telling could open the door for others.
The pace development in the first half-mile will be crucial - if it becomes a crawl, the hold-up horses gain a significant advantage.
Numitor's behaviour and willingness to race - given his unpredictable nature, his attitude on the day will determine his chance completely.

runners_data.spotlight: Good ground for all seven of his races; won in small fields for a maiden (here) and a novice hurdle; ran creditably in 3m/2m7f handicaps on last two outings, seemingly needing some respite from the handicapper, who's not made much of a reaction, but this field may offer him a better chance.

races.paceDynamic: Queens Venture and Grangeclare Diego will dispute the early lead, with Queens Venture likely to get first run having shown more recent pace. With only six runners over this staying trip, the pace will be honest but not furious, allowing the field to stay reasonably compact through the middle stages. I'm A Starman will track prominently behind the leaders while the three hold-up horses (Court In A Storm, Gold For Alec, Block Rockin Beats) will need to find their rhythm from the back. This moderate gallop over 3m1½f strongly favours prominent runners who can stay in touch without having too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Queens Venture or I'm A Starman maintain strong positions throughout
scenarios.body: The honest but manageable pace allows horses racing handily to stay in contention without excessive energy expenditure, making their superior tactical position decisive over the extended trip. Hold-up horses find too much ground to make up when the tempo lifts approaching the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Court In A Storm Powers
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong between the two front runners
scenarios.body: A searching gallop plays to Court In A Storm's proven stamina and hold-up style, allowing him to pick off tiring leaders with his superior finishing kick. His recent good form and dual course wins give him the class edge when others weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Queens Venture Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Queens Venture can dictate a steady tempo without serious challenge
scenarios.body: The front runner gets an easy lead and kicks clear when it matters, with her summer wins proving she can control races effectively. The small field size makes it harder for hold-up horses to get competitive positions when she quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners go too fast early and tie up badly
scenarios.body: An unsustainable early battle leaves the door open for the hold-up brigade to sweep past tired leaders in the final half-mile. Block Rockin Beats or Gold For Alec benefit most from this unlikely but possible development.

watchPoints.text: Queens Venture's 131-day layoff could see her blow up if she tries to match Grangeclare Diego's early pace
Gold For Alec's poor record on good ground makes him vulnerable despite his recent Chepstow third
I'm A Starman's age at 13 years old means any jumping errors could prove costly over this extended trip
Block Rockin Beats needs the tongue tie to help his concentration but his recent form suggests deeper issues
Grangeclare Diego's front-running style could set up the race perfectly for closers if he goes too fast early

runners_data.spotlight: Went up 12lb for winning so well at Ludlow in December (2m, good to soft; first run in a tongue-tie) but probably bettered that form when runner-up at Kempton (good), finishing just ahead of Diyaken; solid chance with Aamilah Aswat again aboard.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Risen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent form since blinkers applied but faces tougher opposition than recent Exeter contest
runners_data.comment: This might not be quite so demanding as the Exeter race he contested last time
runners_data.spotlight: Fine on all ground; in a good run of form since the blinkers went on four starts back and this might not be quite so demanding as the Exeter race he contested last time; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Fight My Fire
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse from strong Tizzard yard who should benefit if early pace is strong enough
runners_data.comment: It wasn't a bad run off 2lb higher here last time; shouldn't be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't made any striking progress since winning his maiden in October but it wasn't a bad run off 2lb higher here last time; shouldn't be far away.

runners_data.name: The Tide Turns
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 161 days off with new connections after twice pulling up, major concern
runners_data.comment: Left Gordon Elliott cheaply and twice pulled up since returning from his long absence
runners_data.spotlight: Initially promising over hurdles for Gordon Elliott but lost his way under both codes and left that yard for £1,600 in August 2024; twice pulled up since returning from his long absence.

runners_data.name: Grey Skies
runners_data.note: Front runner with course-and-distance wins but form has dipped in last two starts including should-have-won effort
runners_data.comment: Form dipped in last two races, at Cheltenham then Carlisle where he should have run better
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last summer (2m/2m1f, good), the latest off just a 1lb lower mark; form has dipped in his last two races, at Cheltenham and then Carlisle where he should have run better; absent since November.

runners_data.name: Benvoy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form collapsed after December win despite headgear changes, looks vulnerable off current mark
runners_data.comment: Hard to predict and another change of headgear is tried; risky
runners_data.spotlight: In the reapplied blinkers he beat a fair yardstick at Huntingdon just before Christmas (2m, good to soft) but no shows since then, in a visor and blinkers; looks risky with cheekpieces now turned to.

races.paceDynamic: Diyaken and Grey Skies will contest the lead from flag fall, with both proven front runners likely to set a genuine gallop over this sharp 2m trip. Five horses (Red Rubio, Sun Art, Wild Goose, Phoenix Risen, Benvoy) all want prominent positions, creating inevitable traffic problems and scrimmaging approaching the business end. The pace battle between the two leaders should stretch the field and create gaps, while those trapped in the pack will struggle to get daylight. This setup strongly favours either the pace-setters who can dictate terms or genuine hold-up horses like Fight My Fire and The Tide Turns who can avoid the carnage and finish with one run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Race
scenarios.trigger: If Diyaken or Grey Skies gets soft fractions and kicks clear 2 out
scenarios.body: The winner dictates throughout and has enough left to repel challengers, benefiting from avoiding the prominent pile-up behind. Either Diyaken's class or Grey Skies' course-and-distance suitability proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine and the prominent brigade gets in each other's way
scenarios.body: Fight My Fire times his challenge perfectly from the back as the field spreads out, while The Tide Turns could shock if retaining any ability. The sustained gallop plays into the hands of those with finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the five prominent runners gets first run and avoids trouble
scenarios.body: Wild Goose or Phoenix Risen finds a clean passage through the pack and benefits from race fitness and form momentum. The winner emerges from the jostle with perfect timing and positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and come back to the field dramatically
scenarios.body: Benvoy or Red Rubio benefits from a slowly-run finale when the pace dies, but this seems unlikely given both front runners' honest styles. Would need a tactical error from the leaders to materialize.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early pace battle between Diyaken and Grey Skies potentially compromising both leaders if they go too hard
Monitor the prominent quintet (Red Rubio, Sun Art, Wild Goose, Phoenix Risen, Benvoy) for traffic problems and interference 2-3 out
Check The Tide Turns for any sign of enthusiasm given his recent pulling up and 161-day absence
Observe Wild Goose's jumping in the tongue-tie with inexperienced claimer Aamilah Aswat taking 10lb off
Watch Phoenix Risen's position early as the blinkers may make him keener than usual in a race with genuine pace

runners_data.spotlight: £32,000 yearling; first foal out of a useful 2m4f-3m1f hurdle/chase winner; tongue-tie fitted for debut and market confidence would be welcomed; yard 1-22 in bumpers this season.
